cards.title: One transaction, one effect
items: the domain row and the outbox row commit together in the same JTA transaction — a separate commit for the event loses it, and that lost effect is the bug the pattern exists to remove
the use case owns the transaction: @Transactional on the use-case entry method, never on a resource or a repository; JpaOutbox.persist joins the same EntityManager as the domain write
there is no XA and no distributed transaction: a remote effect is an idempotent async job, and the outbox row is its courier

cards.title: The drain is a bounded job
items: the worker polls the due rows with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, publishes through JMS or HTTP, then marks the row sent — a claimed row is never handed to two workers at once
every job is bounded: batch size, time budget, backoff and a dead-letter; a long operation creates a run row and answers 202 instead of holding the request thread
timers come from @Schedule or ManagedScheduledExecutorService — never new Thread or Executors inside a managed server; the worker is the apps/worker composition root, not a thread in the API

cards.title: At-least-once means idempotent
items: JMS delivery is at-least-once, so every consumer is idempotent: the message carries tenantId, correlationId and an idempotency key, and the consumer deduplicates by that key
the schema backs it up — outbox.idempotency_key is NOT NULL and UNIQUE, and the outbox row also carries tenant_id so the drain stays inside one tenant
a dead-letter row is visible to admins instead of disappearing; outbox idempotency and the two-tenant test are release blockers, and a retry keeps the same key so a replay is a no-op
